KISW.G5.KUSOMA.T1_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.MSA.mastery: Works out what a word means from the passage it is in, and picks the right word for a gap, and does not choose a look-alike word or a word from a nearby sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.KUSOMA.T1_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.mastery: Answers who, where, what happened and what the main message is from a short story, and puts events in order, without using outside knowledge or a detail from the wrong place, in 8 of 10 new questions.

KISW.G5.KUANDI.T1_INSHA_YA_WASIFU.AINA_Z.mastery: Tells a short text that describes a person (wasifu), one that tells events in order (masimulizi) and one that explains how something is done or what it is (maelezo), in 8 of 10 new short texts.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T1_AINA_ZA_NOMINO.PEKEE.mastery: Picks the proper noun (the particular name of a person, place, river, school, month) from a sentence and uses one to fill a gap, and does not choose a common noun, a job title or the first word of the sentence, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T1_AINA_ZA_NOMINO_2.KAWAI.mastery: Picks the common noun (the general name of a kind of person, place, animal or thing) from a sentence and uses one to fill a gap, and does not choose a name, a verb or an adjective, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

KISW.G5.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_KINA.KAMUSI.mastery: Puts words in dictionary (alphabetical) order, looking at the second and third letter when the first letters match, and finds the word that comes first or comes next, in 8 of 10 new lists.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T2_AINA_ZA_NOMINO.WINGI.mastery: Gives the plural of a noun in the classes ki-vi, m-wa, m-mi, ji-ma and n (kitabu-vitabu, mtoto-watoto, mti-miti, jiwe-mawe, kalamu-kalamu) and uses it in a sentence, without leaving the noun unchanged or putting on the wrong prefix, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T2_AINA_ZA_NOMINO_2.VITEN.mastery: Tells a verbal noun (kusoma, kucheza, kulima: the verb with ku- used as a noun) from an ordinary verb or the doer noun, and uses it in a sentence, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

KISW.G5.KUSIKI.T3_VITENDAWILI.VITENDAWIL.mastery: Picks the kitendawili (riddle) from a methali, a nahau and an ordinary sentence, and gives the answer to a known riddle, in 8 of 10 new items. Setting and guessing riddles aloud (outcome b) stays with the teacher.

KISW.G5.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.UFA.mastery: Names what a fluent reader does (clear sounds, a fitting speed, a fitting voice, a pause at the koma and the kikomo) and does not take speed or loudness for fluency, in 8 of 10 new items. Reading a passage aloud at a fitting speed, with the voice and signs (outcomes c to e) is judged by a teacher listening.

KISW.G5.KUANDI.T3_KUANDIKA_KWA_TARAKIL.S.mastery: Names the parts of a computer used to type (kibodi, kipanya, skrini, kitengo kikuu, kichapishi) and what each does, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T3_AINA_ZA_NOMINO.MAKUNDI.mastery: Names the usual group noun for people and things (umati wa watu, jeshi la askari, msafara wa magari, mkungu wa ndizi, tita la kuni) and does not use one group word for every group or a single noun, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T3_AINA_ZA_NOMINO_2.AMBAT.mastery: Tells a compound noun (mwanafunzi, mwanahabari, mwanamichezo: nouns built from two words joined into one) from a simple noun and uses one in a sentence, and does not write it as two separate words, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T3_AINA_ZA_NOMINO_3.DHAHA.mastery: Picks the abstract noun (upendo, ukarimu, amani, furaha, uongo: an idea or feeling that cannot be touched), gives it from the person or verb it comes from, and uses it in a sentence, without choosing a thing or a verb, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T3_UAKIFISHI.UAKIFISHI.mastery: Chooses the sentence with the right capital letter, koma, kikomo (full stop) and kiulizi (question mark), and finds the one mistake in a short note, in 8 of 10 new sentences.

KISW.G5.KUSIKI.T4_MANENO_YA_HESHIMA_NA.H.mastery: Names family relations and the greeting that shows respect (shangazi, mjomba, binamu, bibi, shikamoo, marahaba) and does not swap the mother's side and the father's side, in 8 of 10 new items. Using the words in daily talk (outcome b) stays with the teacher.

KISW.G5.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_MAPANA.USAL.mastery: Chooses the safe step when using a phone, tablet or computer (keep the password secret, ask an adult before an unknown link, use a safe site) and not the unsafe one, in 8 of 10 new situations.

KISW.G5.KUANDI.T4_BARUAPEPE.BARUAPEPE.mastery: Names the parts of an email (anayepokea, mada, salamu, ujumbe, hitimisho, jina la mwandishi) and puts the right words in the right part, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T4_NGELI_YA_I_ZI.I_ZI.mastery: Knows nouns that belong to I-ZI (nyumba, meza, barabara, taa, simu), gives the subject prefix i- for one and zi- for many, and makes the plural of a sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.KUSIKI.T5_METHALI.METHALI.mastery: Completes a methali about hard work (haba na haba hujaza kibaba) and says what it means, and does not read it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items. Using a methali when speaking (outcome c) stays with the teacher.

KISW.G5.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.SHA.mastery: Counts the mizani (syllables) in a line by counting vowel sounds, and finds the vina (the matching endings of lines), and does not count words or letters, in 8 of 10 new lines.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T5_NGELI_YA_U_ZI.U_ZI.mastery: Knows nouns that belong to U-ZI (ukuta, wimbo, ubao, ufunguo, uso), gives u- for one and zi- for many, and gives the plural noun (ukuta-kuta, wimbo-nyimbo, ubao-mbao), in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T6_NGELI_YA_U_YA.U_YA.mastery: Knows nouns that belong to U-YA (ugonjwa, unyoya, uchungu), gives u- for one and ya- for many, and gives the plural with ma-, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.KUSIKI.T7_NAHAU.NAHAU.mastery: Completes a nahau (kukata tamaa, kupiga moyo konde, kula chumvi) and says what it means, and does not read it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items. Using a nahau when speaking (outcome c) stays with the teacher.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T7_NGELI_YA_KU_KU.KU_KU.mastery: Knows that a verbal noun (kusoma, kucheza, kula) is in KU-KU, takes ku- as its subject prefix, and has no plural, and does not agree it with a- or u-, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.KUSIKI.T8_VISAWE.VISAWE.mastery: Picks the word with almost the same meaning (furaha-bashasha, haraka-upesi) and does not pick the opposite, a related word or a look-alike, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.KUSOMA.T8_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.IGI.mastery: Tells a play from a story (names of speakers, words spoken, directions in brackets), says what a word in the play means, and answers questions about it, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T8_MNYAMBULIKO_WA_VITEN.M.mastery: Tells the three verb forms apart (kutendewa: done for or to someone, kutendeka: can be done or becomes done, kutendana: done to each other) and picks the one a sentence needs, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T9_VINYUME_VYA_VITENZI.VI.mastery: Gives the true opposite of a verb (kufunga-kufungua, kuvaa-kuvua, kuingia-kutoka) and does not use a negative form or a word of similar meaning, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.KUSIKI.T10_TASHBIHI.TASHBIHI.mastery: Completes and picks a simile about behaviour (mkali kama simba, mwoga kama sungura) and does not leave out kama or take it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T10_NYAKATI_NA_HALI.MAZOE.mastery: Uses hu- for what is done every day (Juma hunywa maji) with no subject prefix, and -me- for what is finished (amemaliza), and does not mix them with -na- or -li-, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T11_UKANUSHAJI.UKANUSHAJI.mastery: Makes the negative of a verb in the present (-na-), past (-li-), perfect (-me-) and future (-ta-) for the persons ni-, u-, a-, tu-, m-, wa-, and does not only add si or keep the tense marker, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T11_UKUBWA_NA_UDOGO_WA_N..mastery: Gives the big form (ji-) and the small form (ki-) of nouns that begin with m- (mtoto: jitoto, kitoto; mti: jiti, kijiti; mji: jiji, kijiji), and uses them in a sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.

KISW.G5.SARUFI.T11_UKUBWA_NA_UDOGO_WA_N_.mastery: Gives the big form and the small form of nouns that begin with n- (nyumba: jumba, kijumba; mbwa: jibwa, kibwa), and uses them in a sentence, in 8 of 10 new items.
